units.en: (Gu and Tulubu)
units.literal: (Gu and Tulubu)

units.zh: 王郁耶律圖魯窘
units.en: Wang Yu; Yelu Tulujiong
units.literal: Wang Yu; Yelu Tulujiong

units.zh: 羽之，小字兀裏，字寅底哂。
units.en: Yuzhi, whose childhood name was Wuli and whose courtesy name was Yindi Shen,
units.literal: Yuzhi, childhood name Wuli, courtesy name Yindi Shen.

units.zh: 幼豪爽不群，長嗜學，通諸部語。
units.en: was bold and unconventional as a youth; when grown he devoted himself to learning and mastered the languages of the various tribes.
units.literal: As a child he was bold and unorthodox; when grown he loved learning and mastered the languages of the various tribes.

units.zh: 太祖經營之初，多預軍謀。
units.en: In the early years of Emperor Taizu's state-building, he took part in many military plans.
units.literal: In the early period of the Emperor Taizu's founding efforts, he took part in many military plans.

units.zh: 天顯元年，渤海平，立皇太子為東丹王，以羽之為中臺省右次相。
units.en: In the first year of Tianxian, after Bohai was pacified, the heir apparent was installed as King of Eastern Dan and Yuzhi was appointed Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Court.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianxian, when Bohai was pacified, the heir apparent was installed as King of Eastern Dan, and Yuzhi was made Right Vice Chancellor of the Central Court.

units.zh: 時人心未安，左大相叠剌不逾月薨，羽之蒞事勤恪，威信並行。
units.en: Popular sentiment was still unsettled at the time; the Left Grand Chancellor Diechi died within a month of taking office, yet Yuzhi handled affairs with diligence and rigor, and authority and trust went hand in hand.
units.literal: At that time popular sentiment was still unsettled; the Left Grand Chancellor Diechi died within a month of taking office, but Yuzhi conducted affairs with diligence and strictness, and authority and trust went hand in hand.

units.zh: 太宗即位，上表曰：「我大聖天皇始有東土，擇賢輔以撫斯民，不以臣愚而任之，國家利害，敢不以聞。
units.en: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Yuzhi submitted a memorial that read: "Our Great Sage Heavenly Emperor first secured the eastern lands and chose worthy ministers to govern the people. Though he did not regard me as capable, he still entrusted me with office; how could I fail to speak of what helps or harms the state?
units.literal: When Emperor Taizong acceded, he submitted a memorial saying: "Our Great Sage Heavenly Emperor first gained the eastern lands and chose worthy men to comfort the people. Though he did not regard this subject as wise, he still entrusted me with office; the gains and losses of the state—how dare I not report them?

units.zh: 渤海昔畏南朝，阻險自衛，居忽汗城。
units.en: Bohai once feared the Southern Court, held itself behind natural barriers, and made its seat at Hohan.
units.literal: Bohai in the past feared the Southern Court, relied on natural barriers for self-defense, and dwelt at Hohan city.

units.zh: 今去上京遼邈，既不為用，又不罷戍，果何為哉？
units.en: It now lies far from the Supreme Capital, yet we neither put it to use nor withdraw the garrisons—what is the point?
units.literal: Now it lies far from the Supreme Capital; it is neither useful nor are the garrisons withdrawn—what purpose does this serve?

units.zh: 先帝因彼離心，乘釁而動，故不戰而克。
units.en: The late emperor took advantage of their divided loyalties and struck when the moment was ripe, and so conquered them without a battle.
units.literal: The late emperor, because their hearts were divided, seized the opportunity and moved; therefore he conquered without fighting.

units.zh: 天授人與，彼一時也。
units.en: Heaven granted the opportunity and men seized it—that was a moment that will not return.
units.literal: Heaven bestowed and men granted—that was a moment in time.

units.zh: 遺種浸以蕃息，今居遠境，恐為後患。
units.en: Their surviving people have gradually multiplied; living now on distant frontiers, they may yet become a future threat.
units.literal: The surviving people have gradually multiplied; now they dwell on distant borders and may become a later trouble.

units.zh: 梁水之地，乃其故鄉，地衍土活，有木鐵鹽魚之利。
units.en: The Liangshui region is their ancestral homeland: the land is broad, the soil fertile, and it offers timber, iron, salt, and fish.
units.literal: The land of Liangshui is their old homeland; the soil is broad and fertile, and there are advantages in timber, iron, salt, and fish.

units.zh: 乘其微弱，徙還其民，萬世長策也。
units.en: While they are still weak, move their people back home—that is a policy for the ages.
units.literal: Taking advantage of their weakness, relocate their people back—a long-term policy for ten thousand generations.

units.zh: 彼得故鄉，又獲木鐵鹽魚之饒，必安居樂業。
units.en: Once they regain their homeland and the bounty of timber, iron, salt, and fish, they will surely settle down and prosper.
units.literal: When they regain their homeland and also obtain the abundance of timber, iron, salt, and fish, they will surely settle in peace and take joy in their work.

units.zh: 然後選徒以翼吾左，突厥、党項、室韋夾輔吾右，可以坐制南邦，混一天下，成聖祖未集之功，貽後世無疆之福。」
units.en: Then choose settlers to strengthen our left, with the Turks, Tanguts, and Shiwei flanking our right, and we can hold the southern states in check from a secure position, unite the realm, finish the work our sage founder left incomplete, and bequeath boundless blessings to posterity."
units.literal: Then select settlers to strengthen our left flank; with the Turks, Tanguts, and Shiwei flanking our right, we can control the southern states from a fixed position, unite all under Heaven, complete the unfinished work of the sage ancestor, and bequeath boundless blessings to later generations."

units.zh: 表奏，帝嘉納之。
units.en: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor praised it and accepted his advice.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.

units.zh: 是歲，詔徙東丹國民於梁水，時稱其善。
units.en: That year an edict moved the people of Eastern Dan to Liangshui, and contemporaries praised the policy as wise.
units.literal: That year an edict ordered the people of Eastern Dan relocated to Liangshui; at the time his policy was praised as good.

units.zh: 人皇王奔唐，羽之鎮撫國人，一切如故。
units.en: When the Renhuang King fled to Tang, Yuzhi pacified the populace and kept everything as it had been.
units.literal: When the Renhuang King fled to Tang, Yuzhi pacified the people of the state and kept everything as before.

units.zh: 以功加守太傅，遷中臺省左相。
units.en: For his service he was additionally appointed Acting Grand Tutor and promoted to Left Chancellor of the Central Court.
units.literal: For his merit he was additionally made Acting Grand Tutor and transferred to Left Chancellor of the Central Court.

units.zh: 會同初，以冊禮赴闕，加特進。
units.en: At the opening of the Huitong era he went to court for the enthronement ceremonies and was granted the rank of Special Advancement.
units.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, he went to court for the investiture rites and was given the special advancement rank.

units.zh: 表奏左次相渤海蘇貪墨不法事，卒。
units.en: He submitted a memorial exposing the corruption and lawlessness of Su of Bohai, the Left Vice Chancellor, then died.
units.literal: He memorialized reporting that Su of Bohai, the Left Vice Chancellor, was corrupt and lawless, then died.

units.zh: 子和裏，終東京留守。
units.en: His son Heli eventually served as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: His son Heli ended as Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 耶律鐸臻，字敵輦，六院部人。
units.en: Yelu Duozhen, whose courtesy name was Dinian, came from the Six Yuan Divisions.
units.literal: Yelu Duozhen, courtesy name Dinian, was a man of the Six Yuan Divisions.

units.zh: 祖蒲古只，遙輦氏時再為本部夷離堇。
units.en: His grandfather Pugu Zhi had twice served as tribal chieftain of their division under the Yaolian clan.
units.literal: His grandfather Pugu Zhi twice served as Yilijin of this division in the time of the Yaolian clan.

units.zh: 耶律狼德等既害玄祖，暴橫益肆。
units.en: After Yelu Langde and his faction murdered the Mysterious Ancestor, their violence and arrogance grew ever bolder.
units.literal: After Yelu Langde and others had killed the Mysterious Ancestor, their violence and arrogance grew ever more unrestrained.

units.zh: 蒲古只以計誘其黨，悉誅夷之。
units.en: Pugu Zhi lured their faction into a trap by stratagem and put them all to death.
units.literal: Pugu Zhi by stratagem lured out their faction and executed them all.

units.zh: 鐸臻幼有誌節，太祖為於越，常居左右。
units.en: Duozhen showed moral resolve even as a youth; while Emperor Taizu still held the title of Yuyue, he kept Duozhen constantly at his side.
units.literal: Duozhen in youth had resolve and integrity; when the Emperor Taizu was Yuyue, he constantly attended at his side.

units.zh: 後即位，梁人遣使求轅軸材，太祖難之。
units.en: After he took the throne, Liang sent envoys requesting timber for chariot axles, and Emperor Taizu was at a loss how to respond.
units.literal: Later, when he took the throne, the people of Liang sent envoys requesting axle-hub timber, and the Emperor Taizu found it difficult.

units.zh: 鐸臻曰：「梁名求材，實覘吾輕重。
units.en: Duozhen said, "Liang claims to want timber, but in truth they are testing our strength.
units.literal: Duozhen said: "Liang asks for timber in name, but in fact they are probing our strength.

units.zh: 宜答曰：『材之所生，必深山窮谷，有神司之，須白鼻赤驢禱祠，然後可伐。』
units.en: We should answer that the timber grows only in deep mountains and remote valleys, that a spirit oversees it, and that it cannot be cut until one has prayed with a white-nosed red donkey.
units.literal: We should answer: 'Where the timber grows must be deep mountains and remote valleys; a spirit oversees it, and one must pray with a white-nosed red donkey before it can be cut.'

units.zh: 如此，則其語自塞矣。」
units.en: If we say that, their request will collapse of its own absurdity."
units.literal: In this way their words will choke themselves off."

units.zh: 已而果然。
units.en: And so it proved.
units.literal: Before long it proved exactly so.

units.zh: 天贊三年，將伐渤海，鐸臻諫曰：「陛下先事渤海，則西夏必躡吾後。
units.en: In the third year of Tianzan, as the emperor prepared to attack Bohai, Duozhen remonstrated: "If Your Majesty strikes at Bohai first, Western Xia will surely fall upon our rear.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianzan, when he was about to attack Bohai, Duozhen remonstrated: "If Your Majesty deals with Bohai first, Western Xia will surely tread on our rear.

units.zh: 請先西討，庶無後顧憂。」
units.en: Attack the west first, so that we need not fear what lies behind us."
units.literal: Please attack west first, so that there may be no worry behind."

units.zh: 太祖從之。
units.en: Emperor Taizu followed his counsel.
units.literal: The Emperor Taizu followed his advice.

units.zh: 及淳欽皇后稱制，惡鐸臻，囚之，誓曰：「鐵鎖朽，當釋汝！」
units.en: When Empress Chunqin assumed the regency, she took a dislike to Duozhen and imprisoned him, swearing, "When the iron chains rust through, I shall release you!"
units.literal: When Empress Chunqin assumed regency, she disliked Duozhen, imprisoned him, and swore: "When the iron chains rot, I shall release you!"

units.zh: 既而召之，使者欲去鎖，鐸臻辭曰：「鐵未朽，可釋乎？」
units.en: Later she summoned him; when the messenger moved to remove his chains, Duozhen refused: "The iron has not yet rusted—may I be released?"
units.literal: Later she summoned him; the envoy wished to remove the locks, but Duozhen declined: "The iron has not rotted—may I be released?"

units.zh: 後聞，嘉嘆，趣召釋之。
units.en: When she heard of this, she marveled and sighed with approval, and at once ordered him freed.
units.literal: When she heard of this afterward, she praised and sighed, and urgently summoned and released him.

units.zh: 天顯二年卒。
units.en: He died in the second year of Tianxian.
units.literal: He died in the second year of Tianxian.

units.zh: 弟古、突呂不。
units.en: His younger brothers were Gu and Tulubu.
units.literal: His younger brothers were Gu and Tulubu.

units.zh: 古，字涅剌昆，初名霞馬葛。
units.en: Gu, whose courtesy name was Nielakun and whose original name was Xiamage,
units.literal: Gu, courtesy name Nielakun, original name Xiamage.

units.zh: 太祖為於越，嘗從略地山右。
units.en: when Emperor Taizu was still Yuyue, once accompanied him in campaigns west of the mountains.
units.literal: when the Emperor Taizu was Yuyue, once followed him in raiding the lands west of the mountains.

units.zh: 會李克用於雲州，古侍，克用異之曰：「是兒骨相非常，不宜使在左右。」
units.en: He met Li Keyong at Yunzhou while attending the emperor; Keyong remarked in wonder, "This boy's bearing is extraordinary—he should not be kept close at hand."
units.literal: He met Li Keyong at Yunzhou; Gu attended him, and Keyong marveled, saying: "This boy's bone structure is extraordinary; he should not be kept at one's side."

units.zh: 以故太祖頗忌之。
units.en: For this reason Emperor Taizu grew somewhat wary of him.
units.literal: For this reason the Emperor Taizu came to be somewhat wary of him.

units.zh: 時方西討，諸弟亂作，聞變，太祖問古與否，曰無。
units.en: While the army was campaigning in the west, the emperor's younger brothers rose in revolt. On hearing the news, Emperor Taizu asked whether Gu had taken part; he was told no.
units.literal: At that time they were campaigning west; the emperor's younger brothers rose in revolt. On hearing of the disturbance, the Emperor Taizu asked whether Gu was involved; the answer was no.

units.zh: 喜曰：「吾無患矣！」
units.en: The emperor rejoiced: "Then I have nothing to fear!"
units.literal: He rejoiced: "I have no worry!"

units.zh: 趣召古議。
units.en: He at once summoned Gu to counsel him.
units.literal: He urgently summoned Gu to deliberate.

units.zh: 古陳殄滅之策，後皆如言，以故錫賚甚厚。
units.en: Gu laid out a plan for their destruction, and events afterward unfolded exactly as he had said; for this the emperor lavished rewards upon him.
units.literal: Gu set forth a plan for their extermination; afterward events all matched his words, and for this reason rewards were very generous.

units.zh: 神冊末，南伐，以古佐右皮室詳穩老古，與唐兵戰於雲碧店，老古中流矢，傷甚，太祖疑古陰害之。
units.en: At the end of the Shence era, during the southern campaign, Gu served as deputy to Laogu, commander of the Right Pishi Division; they fought Tang forces at Yunbi, where Laogu was struck by an arrow and badly wounded. Emperor Taizu suspected that Gu had plotted against him in secret.
units.literal: At the end of Shence, on the southern campaign, Gu was made assistant to Laogu, Xiangwen of the Right Pishi Division; they fought Tang troops at Yunbi post, Laogu was struck by a flying arrow and badly wounded, and the Emperor Taizu suspected Gu of secretly harming him.

units.zh: 古知上意，跪曰：「陛下疑臣恥居老古麾下耶？
units.en: Gu understood the emperor's suspicion, knelt, and said, "Does Your Majesty think I was ashamed to serve under Laogu?
units.literal: Gu knew the emperor's mind, knelt, and said: "Does Your Majesty suspect that this subject was ashamed to serve under Laogu?

units.zh: 及今老古在，請遣使問之。」
units.en: Laogu is still alive—send someone to ask him."
units.literal: Since Laogu is still alive, please send an envoy to ask him."

units.zh: 太祖使問老古，對曰：「臣於古無可疑者。」
units.en: Emperor Taizu did so; Laogu replied, "I have no suspicion of Gu whatsoever."
units.literal: The Emperor Taizu sent to ask Laogu, who answered: "This subject has nothing doubtful about Gu."

units.zh: 上意乃釋。
units.en: The emperor's doubts were dispelled.
units.literal: The emperor's mind was then released.

units.zh: 老古卒，遂以古為右皮室詳穩。
units.en: After Laogu died, Gu was appointed commander of the Right Pishi Division.
units.literal: When Laogu died, Gu was then made Xiangwen of the Right Pishi Division.

units.zh: 既卒，太祖謂左右曰：「古死，猶長松自倒，非吾伐之也。」
units.en: After his death Emperor Taizu told those around him, "When Gu died, it was like a great pine toppling of its own weight—not because I felled it."
units.literal: After he died, the Emperor Taizu said to those around him: "When Gu died, it was like a tall pine falling of itself—not because I cut it down."

units.zh: 突呂不，字鐸袞，幼聰敏嗜學。
units.en: Tulubu, whose courtesy name was Duogun, was clever and devoted to learning from childhood.
units.literal: Tulubu, courtesy name Duogun, in youth was clever and loved learning.

units.zh: 事太祖見器重。
units.en: In serving Emperor Taizu he won deep trust.
units.literal: In serving the Emperor Taizu he was regarded with esteem.

units.zh: 及制契丹大字，突呂不贊成為多。
units.en: When the Khitan large script was created, Tulubu contributed more than anyone else to bringing it to completion.
units.literal: When the Khitan large script was devised, Tulubu contributed much to its completion.

units.zh: 未幾，為文班林牙，領國子博士、知制誥。
units.en: Before long he was made Linya of the Civil Class and concurrently served as Doctor of the National University and Drafter of Imperial Edicts.
units.literal: Before long he became Linya of the Civil Class, and concurrently held the posts of Doctor of the National University and Drafter of Imperial Edicts.

units.zh: 明年，受詔撰決獄法。
units.en: The following year he received an edict to draft the law on judicial decisions.
units.literal: The next year he received an edict to compile the law on deciding cases.

units.zh: 太祖略燕，詔與皇太子及王郁攻定州。
units.en: When Emperor Taizu overran Yan, he was ordered to attack Dingzhou with the heir apparent and Wang Yu.
units.literal: When the Emperor Taizu overran Yan, he was ordered to attack Dingzhou together with the heir apparent and Wang Yu.

units.zh: 師還至順州，幽州馬步軍指揮使王千率眾來襲，突呂不射其馬躓，擒之。
units.en: On the army's return to Shunzhou, Wang Qian, commander of the Youzhou horse and foot forces, led a raid; Tulubu shot his horse from under him and took him prisoner.
units.literal: On the army's return to Shunzhou, Wang Qian, commander of the Youzhou horse and foot forces, led troops to attack; Tulubu shot his horse so that it stumbled and captured him.

units.zh: 天贊二年，皇子堯骨為大元帥，突呂不為副，既克平州，進軍燕、趙，攻下曲陽、北平。
units.en: In the second year of Tianzan, Prince Yaogu served as grand marshal with Tulubu as his deputy; after taking Pingzhou they advanced into Yan and Zhao and captured Quyang and Beiping.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianzan, the prince Yaogu was Grand Marshal and Tulubu was his deputy; after they took Pingzhou they advanced into Yan and Zhao and captured Quyang and Beiping.

units.zh: 至易州，易人來拒，逾濠而陣。
units.en: At Yizhou the defenders came out to resist, forming their lines beyond the moat.
units.literal: Reaching Yizhou, the people of Yi came out to resist and formed battle lines beyond the moat.

units.zh: 李景章出降，言城中人無鬥志。
units.en: Li Jingzhang came out to surrender and reported that the city had lost the will to fight.
units.literal: Li Jingzhang came out to surrender and said the people in the city had no fighting spirit.

units.zh: 大元帥將修攻具，突呂不諫曰：「我師遠來，人馬疲憊，勢不可久留。」
units.en: The grand marshal was about to prepare siege engines when Tulubu remonstrated: "Our army has marched far; men and horses are exhausted—we cannot afford to linger."
units.literal: The Grand Marshal was about to prepare siege engines; Tulubu remonstrated: "Our army has come from afar; men and horses are weary—the situation cannot allow a long stay."

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: The assault was called off.
units.literal: He then stopped.

units.zh: 軍還，大元帥以其謀聞，太祖大悅，賜賚優渥。
units.en: On the army's return the grand marshal reported his counsel to the throne; Emperor Taizu was greatly pleased and rewarded him lavishly.
units.literal: When the army returned, the Grand Marshal reported his counsel; the Emperor Taizu was greatly pleased and bestowed generous rewards.

units.zh: 車駕西征，突呂不與大元帥為先鋒，伐党項有功，太祖犒師水精山。
units.en: On the western campaign Tulubu and the grand marshal led the vanguard; their attack on the Tanguts succeeded, and Emperor Taizu feasted the army at Crystal Mountain.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Tulubu and the Grand Marshal served as vanguard; in attacking the Tanguts they had merit, and the Emperor Taizu feasted the army at Shuijing Mountain.

units.zh: 大元帥東歸，突呂不留屯西南部，復討党項，多獲而還。
units.en: When the grand marshal returned east, Tulubu remained to garrison the southwest, raided the Tanguts again, took many captives, and returned.
units.literal: The Grand Marshal returned east; Tulubu remained to garrison the southwestern region, again attacked the Tanguts, took many captives, and returned.

units.zh: 太祖東伐，大諲譔降而復叛，攻之，突呂不先登。
units.en: On Emperor Taizu's eastern campaign, Dayinzan surrendered and then rebelled again; in the assault Tulubu was first over the wall.
units.literal: When the Emperor Taizu campaigned east, Dayinzan surrendered then rebelled again; in the attack Tulubu was first to scale the walls.

units.zh: 渤海平，承詔銘太祖功德於永興殿壁。
units.en: After Bohai was pacified, he received an edict to inscribe Emperor Taizu's achievements on the walls of the Hall of Everlasting Prosperity.
units.literal: When Bohai was pacified, he received an edict to inscribe the Emperor Taizu's merit on the walls of the Yongxing Hall.

units.zh: 班師，已下州郡往往復叛，突呂不從大元帥攻破之。
units.en: On the withdrawal many districts rebelled again; Tulubu followed the grand marshal in reducing them.
units.literal: On the withdrawal, prefectures and districts below often rebelled again; Tulubu followed the Grand Marshal in reducing them.

units.zh: 淳欽皇后稱制，有飛語中傷者，後怒，突呂不懼而亡。
units.en: When Empress Chunqin assumed the regency, slanders reached her ears; enraged, she drove Tulubu to flee in fear.
units.literal: When Empress Chunqin assumed regency, there were slanders that wounded him; the empress was angry, and Tulubu, in fear, fled.

units.zh: 太宗知其無罪，召還。
units.en: Emperor Taizong knew he was innocent and recalled him.
units.literal: Emperor Taizong knew he was guiltless and summoned him back.

units.zh: 天顯三年，討烏古部，俘獲甚眾。
units.en: In the third year of Tianxian he attacked the Wugu tribe and took a great many captives.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianxian he attacked the Wugu tribe and took very many captives.

units.zh: 伐唐，以突呂不為左翼，攻唐軍霞沙寨，降之。
units.en: In the campaign against Tang he commanded the left wing, attacked the Tang garrison at Xiasha, and received its surrender.
units.literal: In the campaign against Tang, Tulubu was made left wing; he attacked the Tang army's Xiasha stockade and received its surrender.

units.zh: 十一年，送晉主石敬瑭入洛。
units.en: In the eleventh year he escorted the Jin ruler Shi Jingtang into Luoyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh year he escorted the Jin ruler Shi Jingtang into Luoyang.

units.zh: 及大冊，突呂不總禮儀事，加特進檢校太尉。
units.en: At the grand enthronement ceremony he oversaw all ritual affairs and was granted the ranks of Special Advancement and Acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: At the great investiture he oversaw ritual affairs in general and was given Special Advancement and Acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 會同五年卒。
units.en: He died in the fifth year of Huitong.
units.literal: He died in the fifth year of Huitong.

units.zh: 王郁，京兆萬年人，唐義武軍節度使處直之孽子。
units.en: Wang Yu, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the illegitimate son of Wang Chuzhi, military governor of the Yiwu Army under Tang.
units.literal: Wang Yu, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao, was the illegitimate son of Wang Chuzhi, Tang Military Governor of Yiwu Army.

units.zh: 伯父處存鎮義武，卒，三軍推其子郜襲，處直為都知兵馬使。
units.en: His uncle Chucun had governed Yiwu; when he died the army installed his son Gao as successor, with Chuzhi as director of military affairs.
units.literal: His uncle Chucun held Yiwu; when he died the three armies installed his son Gao as successor, and Chuzhi became Director of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 光化三年，梁王朱全忠攻定州，郜遣處直拒於沙河。
units.en: In the third year of Guanghua, Zhu Quanzhong of Liang attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist him at Shahe.
units.literal: In the third year of Guanghua, Liang King Zhu Quanzhong attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist at Shahe.

units.zh: 兵敗，入城逐郜，郜奔太原。
units.en: Defeated in battle, they entered the city and drove Gao out; he fled to Taiyuan.
units.literal: The army was defeated; they entered the city and drove out Gao, and Gao fled to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 亂兵推處直為留後，遣人請事梁王。
units.en: The mutineers installed Chuzhi as acting governor and sent envoys to submit to the Liang court.
units.literal: The mutinous troops installed Chuzhi as acting governor and sent men to request allegiance to the Liang king.

units.zh: 梁與晉王克用絕好，表處直為義武軍節度使。
units.en: Liang broke with Li Keyong of Jin and memorialized Chuzhi as military governor of the Yiwu Army.
units.literal: Liang broke relations with Jin Prince Li Keyong and memorialized Chuzhi as Military Governor of Yiwu Army.

units.zh: 初，郜之亡也，郁從之。
units.en: When Gao first fled, Yu went with him.
units.literal: At first, when Gao fled, Yu followed him.

units.zh: 晉王克用妻以女，用為新州防禦使。
units.en: Li Keyong of Jin gave him his daughter in marriage and appointed him defender of Xinzhou.
units.literal: Jin Prince Li Keyong gave him his daughter in marriage and employed him as Defender of Xinzhou.

units.zh: 處直料晉必討張文禮，鎮亡，則定不獨存，益自疑。
units.en: Chuzhi reckoned that Jin would surely move against Zhang Wenli; if the commandery fell, Dingzhou could not survive on its own, and his suspicions deepened.
units.literal: Chuzhi reckoned that Jin would surely punish Zhang Wenli; if the commandery perished, Dingzhou could not stand alone, and he grew ever more suspicious.

units.zh: 陰使郁北導契丹入塞，以牽晉兵，且許為嗣。
units.en: He secretly sent Yu north to guide the Khitan across the border and tie down Jin's forces, promising him the succession as well.
units.literal: He secretly sent Yu north to guide the Khitan into the passes, to tie down Jin's army, and also promised him the succession.

units.zh: 郁自奔晉，常恐失父心，得使，大喜。
units.en: Yu had fled to Jin and constantly feared he had lost his father's favor; when this mission came he was overjoyed.
units.literal: Yu had himself fled to Jin and constantly feared losing his father's favor; when he received this mission he was greatly pleased.

units.zh: 神冊六年，奉表送款，舉室來降，太祖以為養子。
units.en: In the sixth year of Shence he submitted a memorial of allegiance and came over with his entire household; Emperor Taizu adopted him as a son.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Shence he submitted a memorial offering allegiance; his whole household came to surrender, and the Emperor Taizu took him as an adopted son.

units.zh: 未幾，郁兄都囚父，自為留後，帝遣郁從皇太子討之。
units.en: Before long Yu's elder brother Du imprisoned their father and made himself acting governor; the emperor sent Yu with the heir apparent to punish him.
units.literal: Before long Yu's elder brother Du imprisoned their father and installed himself as acting governor; the emperor sent Yu to follow the heir apparent in punishing him.

units.zh: 至定州，都堅壁不出，掠居民而還。
units.en: At Dingzhou, Du held the walls and refused to come out; they plundered the countryside and withdrew.
units.literal: Reaching Dingzhou, Du held fast behind the walls and would not come out; they plundered the inhabitants and returned.

units.zh: 明年，從皇太子攻鎮州，遇唐兵於定州，破之。
units.en: The following year he followed the heir apparent against Zhenzhou, met Tang forces at Dingzhou, and routed them.
units.literal: The next year he followed the heir apparent in attacking Zhenzhou; they met Tang troops at Dingzhou and defeated them.

units.zh: 天贊二年秋，郁及阿古只略地燕、趙，攻下磁窯務。
units.en: In the autumn of the second year of Tianzan, Yu and Aguzhi raided Yan and Zhao and captured Ciyaowu.
units.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Tianzan, Yu and Aguzhi overran the lands of Yan and Zhao and took Ciyaowu.

units.zh: 從太祖平渤海，戰有功，加同政事門下平章事，改崇義軍節度使。
units.en: He followed Emperor Taizu in pacifying Bohai, distinguished himself in battle, was made associate director of the Secretariat with the rank of grand councilor, and was then appointed military governor of the Chongyi Army.
units.literal: Following the Emperor Taizu in pacifying Bohai, he had merit in battle and was made Associate Director of the Secretariat with the rank of Grand Councilor, then transferred to Military Governor of Chongyi Army.

units.zh: 太祖崩，郁與妻會葬，其妻泣訴於淳欽皇后，求歸鄉國，許之。
units.en: When Emperor Taizu died, Yu and his wife attended the funeral; his wife wept before Empress Chunqin and begged to return home, and the empress granted her request.
units.literal: When the Emperor Taizu died, Yu and his wife attended the funeral; his wife wept and appealed to Empress Chunqin, asking to return to their native land, and permission was granted.

units.zh: 郁奏曰：「臣本唐主之婿，主已被弒，此行夫妻豈能相保？
units.en: Yu submitted a memorial: "I was once the son-in-law of a Tang ruler; my lord has already been murdered—on this journey how can my wife and I keep each other safe?
units.literal: Yu memorialized: "This subject was originally the son-in-law of the Tang ruler; my lord has already been assassinated—on this journey how can husband and wife protect each other?

units.zh: 願常侍太后。」
units.en: I beg to remain in constant attendance upon the empress dowager."
units.literal: I wish to attend the empress dowager constantly."

units.zh: 後喜曰：「漢人中，惟王郎最忠孝。」
units.en: The empress was delighted: "Among the Han, none is more loyal and filial than Lord Wang."
units.literal: The empress rejoiced: "Among the Han, only Lord Wang is most loyal and filial."

units.zh: 以太祖嘗與李克用約為兄弟故也。
units.en: This was because Emperor Taizu had once sworn brotherhood with Li Keyong.
units.literal: This was because the Emperor Taizu had once sworn brotherhood with Li Keyong.

units.zh: 尋加政事令。
units.en: Before long he was additionally appointed director of government affairs.
units.literal: Before long he was additionally made Director of Government Affairs.

units.zh: 還宜州，卒。
units.en: He returned to Yizhou, where he died.
units.literal: He returned to Yizhou and died.

units.zh: 耶律圖魯窘，字阿魯隱，肅祖子洽瑽之孫，勇而有謀略。
units.en: Yelu Tulujiong, whose courtesy name was Aluyin, was the grandson of Qiazhen, a son of Emperor Suzu; he was courageous and resourceful in counsel.
units.literal: Yelu Tulujiong, courtesy name Aluyin, was the grandson of Qiazhen, son of Emperor Suzu; he was brave and possessed stratagems.

units.zh: 太宗立晉之役，其父敵魯古為五院夷離堇，歿於兵，帝即以其職授圖魯窘。
units.en: During Emperor Taizong's campaign to establish the Later Jin state, his father Dilugu served as chieftain of the Five Yuan Divisions and died in battle; the emperor at once gave Tulujiong his father's post.
units.literal: In Emperor Taizong's campaign to establish Jin, his father Dilugu was Yilijin of the Five Yuan Divisions and died in battle; the emperor at once gave Tulujiong his post.

units.zh: 會同元年，改北院大王，嘗屏左右與議大事，占對合上意。
units.en: In the first year of Huitong he was made king of the Northern Court; he would dismiss his attendants to discuss weighty matters, and his counsel always matched the emperor's intent.
units.literal: In the first year of Huitong he was made King of the Northern Court; he would dismiss attendants to discuss great affairs, and his responses matched the emperor's intent.

units.zh: 從討石重貴，杜重威擁十萬餘眾拒滹沱橋，力戰數日，不得進。
units.en: In the campaign against Shi Chonggui, Du Chongwei held more than a hundred thousand men at the Hutuo bridge; after days of fierce fighting the army could not break through.
units.literal: Following the campaign against Shi Chonggui, Du Chongwei held more than a hundred thousand men to block the Hutuo bridge; they fought fiercely for several days but could not advance.

units.zh: 帝曰：「兩軍爭渡，人馬疲矣，計安出？」
units.en: The emperor said, "Both armies are fighting for the crossing; men and horses are exhausted—what is to be done?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "The two armies contend for the crossing; men and horses are weary—what plan should be adopted?"

units.zh: 諸將請緩師，為後圖，帝然之。
units.en: The generals urged slowing the advance to regroup; the emperor agreed.
units.literal: The generals asked to slow the army and plan for later; the emperor approved.

units.zh: 圖魯窘厲色進曰：「臣愚竊以為陛下樂於安逸，則謹守四境可也；
units.en: Tulujiong stepped forward with a stern expression and said, "Your humble servant ventures to think that if Your Majesty delights in ease, then guarding the four borders is enough;
units.literal: Tulujiong advanced with stern countenance and said: "This foolish subject ventures to think that if Your Majesty delights in ease, then strictly guarding the four borders would suffice;

units.zh: 既欲擴大疆宇，出師遠攻，詎能無廑聖慮。
units.en: but if you wish to expand the realm and send the army on distant campaigns, how can Your Majesty not weigh every consequence with care?
units.literal: if you wish to expand territory and send the army on distant attack, how can there be no anxious imperial deliberation?

units.zh: 若中路而止，適為賊利，則必陷南京，夷屬邑。
units.en: If we halt halfway, we only strengthen the enemy; the Southern Capital will fall and our dependent districts will be laid waste.
units.literal: If we halt halfway, that would only profit the enemy; then the Southern Capital would surely fall and dependent districts be destroyed.

units.zh: 若此，則爭戰未已，吾民無奠枕之期矣。
units.en: Then the fighting will never end, and our people will never know a night of peaceful sleep.
units.literal: If so, fighting would not cease and our people would have no time to lay their heads on pillows in peace.

units.zh: 且彼步我騎，何慮不克！
units.en: They fight on foot and we fight on horseback—why should we fear defeat?
units.literal: Moreover, they are infantry and we are cavalry—what worry is there of not conquering!

units.zh: 況漢人足力弱而行緩，如選輕銳騎先絕其餉道，則事蔑不濟矣。」
units.en: The Han march slowly on weak legs; send light, elite cavalry to cut their supply lines first, and the matter cannot fail."
units.literal: Moreover the Han have weak legs and slow marching; if we choose light, elite cavalry first to cut off their supply route, then the affair would surely succeed."

units.zh: 帝喜曰：「國強則其人賢，海巨則其魚大。」
units.en: The emperor rejoiced: "When a state is strong, its men are worthy; when the sea is vast, its fish are large."
units.literal: The emperor rejoiced: "When the state is strong its men are worthy; when the sea is vast its fish are large."

units.zh: 於是塞其餉道，數出師以牽撓其勢，重威果降如言。
units.en: They blocked the enemy supply lines and sent out repeated raids to harry their forces; Chongwei surrendered exactly as Tulujiong had predicted.
units.literal: Thereupon they blocked their supply route and sent out troops several times to harass their strength; Chongwei indeed surrendered as he had said.

units.zh: 以功獲賜甚厚。
units.en: For this service he received lavish rewards.
units.literal: For his merit he received very generous rewards.

units.zh: 明年春，卒軍中。
units.en: The following spring he died in camp.
units.literal: In the spring of the next year he died in the army.

units.zh: 論曰：神冊初元，將相大臣拔起風塵之中，翼扶王運，以任職取名者，固一時之材，亦由太祖推誠禦下，不任獨斷，用能總攬群策而為之用歟！
units.en: The commentary says: At the opening of the Shence era, generals and ministers rose from the turmoil of the age to support the royal enterprise. Men who won renown through office were indeed talents of their day, yet it was also because Emperor Taizu dealt sincerely with his subordinates, refused to decide everything alone, and so could gather every counsel and put it to use.
units.literal: The commentary says: At the beginning of Shence, generals, ministers, and great officials were raised from the dust of turmoil to wing and support the royal fortune. Those who gained fame through office were indeed talents of their time, but it was also because the Emperor Taizu treated subordinates with sincerity, did not rely on solitary decisions, and thus could gather all strategies and put them to use!

units.zh: 其投天隙而列功庸，至有心腹、耳目、手足之喻，豈偶然哉！
units.en: That they seized Heaven's openings and won their places of honor, even to the point of being called the ruler's heart, eyes, ears, hands, and feet—could that have been mere chance?
units.literal: That they seized Heaven's openings and ranked their achievements, even to the metaphors of heart, eyes and ears, and hands and feet—was this accidental?

units.zh: 討党項，走敵魯，平剌葛，定渤海，功亦偉矣。
units.en: In subduing the Tanguts, driving off Dilu, pacifying Lage, and settling Bohai, their achievements were likewise magnificent.
units.literal: In punishing the Tanguts, driving off Dilu, pacifying Lage, and settling Bohai, their achievements were also grand.

units.zh: 若默記治獄不冤，頗德持論不撓，延徽立經陳紀，紹勛秉節而死，圖魯窘料敵制勝，豈器博者無近用，道長者其功遠歟？
units.en: Consider Kang Moji, who judged cases without injustice; Pode, who held to his principles without yielding; Han Yanhui, who established institutions and set forth the laws; Shaoxun, who died holding to his integrity; and Tulujiong, who read the enemy and secured victory—are men of broad talent useless in the present, and men of far-reaching vision rewarded only in the long run?
units.literal: As for Moji in governing cases without injustice, Pode in holding to argument without yielding, Yanhui in establishing classics and setting forth institutions, Shaoxun in holding to integrity unto death, and Tulujiong in gauging the enemy and controlling victory—can those whose vessels are broad have no near use, and those whose Way is long have achievements that reach far?

units.zh: 稱為佐命，固宜。
units.en: To call them founders of the dynasty was only fitting.
units.literal: To call them assistants in establishing the mandate was surely fitting.

units.zh: 以天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為御營使。
units.en: Shi Jingtang of Tianxiong became imperial camp commissioner.
units.literal: Tianxiong army military commissioner Shi Jingtang was made imperial camp commissioner.

units.zh: 皇后述律氏居守之際，摘蕃漢精銳為屬珊軍。
units.en: While Empress Shulü kept guard at the capital she selected elite Fan and Han troops for the shushan army.
units.literal: While Empress Shulü held the capital, she picked the finest of Fan and Han troops for the shushan army.

units.zh: 屬珊軍：地皇后屬，二十萬騎。
units.en: The shushan army belonged to the Earth Empress and numbered two hundred thousand riders.
units.literal: Shushan army: belonging to the Earth Empress, two hundred thousand riders.

units.zh: 遼太祖宗室盛強，分叠剌部為二，宮衛內虛，經營四方，未遑鳩集。
units.en: At Liao Taizu's rise the imperial clan was powerful; he divided the Dieci tribe in two, leaving the inner palace guard thin, and while campaigning on every side had no time to muster troops.
units.literal: When Liao Taizu rose the imperial clan was strong; he split the Dieci tribe in two, the inner palace guard was hollow, and while he campaigned on four sides he had no leisure to gather forces.

units.zh: 昭義節度使、侍衛馬軍都指揮使、廣晉府行營都排陣使杜重威，河陽節度使兼奉國左右廂都指揮使、廣晉府行營馬步都虞候侯益，並加檢校太傅。
units.en: Du Chongwei, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, cavalry commander of the palace guard, and chief array marshal of the Guangjin headquarters, and Hou Yi, military commissioner of Heyang, commander of the Fengguo wings, and horse-and-foot chief adjutant of the Guangjin headquarters, were both made honorary grand mentors.
units.literal: Du Chongwei—Military Commissioner of Zhaoyi, Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry, and Chief Array Marshal of the Guangjin Field Headquarters—and Hou Yi—Military Commissioner of Heyang, Commander of the Left and Right Wings of the Fengguo Army, and Horse and Foot Chief Adjutant of the Guangjin Field Headquarters—were both promoted to Honorary Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 初，樞自歙州罷郡歸朝，路經大梁，時硃全忠兵威已振，樞以兄事之，全忠由是重之。
units.en: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.
units.literal: Earlier, when Shu returned to court after leaving his prefecture at She, his route passed through Daliang; Zhu Quanzhong's military prestige was already rising, and Shu treated him as an elder brother—whereupon Quanzhong came to esteem him.

units.zh: 制出，硃全忠保薦之，言樞有經世才，不可棄之嶺表，尋復拜門下侍郎，監修國史，累兼吏部尚書，判度支。
units.en: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed vice minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as minister of personnel, administering the treasury.
units.literal: The appointment was issued; Zhu Quanzhong petitioned in his support, saying Shu had talent to govern the age and must not be abandoned to the Lingnan frontier—soon Shu was again appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery, commissioned to supervise compilation of the dynastic history, and repeatedly served concurrently as Minister of Personnel, administering the treasury.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 時崔胤專政，亦倚全忠，二人因是相結，改樞吏部侍郎。
units.en: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: At the time Cui Yin monopolized power and also leaned on Quanzhong; the two therefore formed an alliance, and Shu was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 崔胤誅，以全忠素厚，相位如故。
units.en: After Cui Yin's execution, Shu's ties to Quanzhong kept him in the chancellorship unchanged.
units.literal: When Cui Yin was executed, because of his longstanding closeness to Quanzhong Shu's chancellorship remained unchanged.

units.zh: 五月，皇弟剌葛、迭剌、寅底石、安端謀反。
units.en: In the fifth month his brothers Cige, Diela, Yindishi, and Anduan conspired to rebel.
units.literal: In the fifth month, his imperial brothers Cige, Diela, Yindishi, and Anduan plotted rebellion.

units.zh: 出剌葛為迭剌部夷離，封粘睦姑為晉國夫人。
units.en: He posted Cige as yilijin of the Diela branch and ennobled Nianmugu as Lady of Jin.
units.literal: Cige was sent out as yilijin of the Diela branch, and Nianmugu was enfeoffed as Lady of Jin.

units.zh: 命弟剌葛分兵攻平州。
units.en: He commanded his brother Cige to split off troops and strike Pingzhou.
units.literal: He ordered his brother Cige to divide forces and attack Pingzhou.

units.zh: 冬十月戊寅，剌葛破平州，還，復與迭剌、寅底石、安端等反。
units.en: In the tenth winter month, on wuyin day, Cige captured Pingzhou and returned, then rebelled again with Diela, Yindishi, Anduan, and others.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on wuyin day, Cige captured Pingzhou and returned, then rebelled again with Diela, Yindishi, Anduan, and others.

units.zh: 甲寅，王師次赤水城，弟剌葛等乞降。
units.en: On jiayin day the imperial forces encamped at Chishui Fort, and his younger brothers Cige and the others pleaded to submit.
units.literal: On jiayin day, the imperial army halted at Chishui Fort; the younger brothers Cige and others begged to surrender.

units.zh: 剌葛等引退，上復數遣使撫慰。
units.en: Cige and the others withdrew, and the Emperor again sent envoys repeatedly to comfort them.
units.literal: Cige and the others withdrew; the Emperor again sent envoys several times to console them.

units.zh: 而剌葛引其眾至乙室堇澱，具天子旗鼓，將自立，皇太后陰遣人諭令避去。
units.en: Meanwhile Cige led his forces to Yishijin Marsh, arrayed the imperial drums and banners, and was about to set himself up as ruler; the Empress Dowager secretly sent word telling him to withdraw.
units.literal: Meanwhile Cige led his host to Yishijin Marsh, equipped with the imperial drums and banners, intending to declare himself ruler; the Empress Dowager secretly sent someone to instruct him to withdraw.

units.zh: 上不忍加誅，乃與諸弟登山刑牲，告天地為誓而赦其罪。
units.en: Unable to bring himself to punish them, he climbed a mountain with his brothers, offered sacrifice, swore before Heaven and Earth, and granted them pardon.
units.literal: The Emperor could not bear to execute them; he therefore climbed a mountain with his brothers, sacrificed animals, announced Heaven and Earth as witnesses to an oath, and pardoned their crime.

units.zh: 北院大王圖魯窘。
units.en: Tulujiong, Northern Chancellery Great King.
units.literal: Northern Chancellery Great King Tulujiong.

units.zh: 右係出肅祖昭烈皇帝。
units.en: Right descent line from Emperor Suzu the Illustrious and Fierce.
units.literal: Right descent line from Emperor Suzu the Illustrious and Fierce.

units.zh: 是月，鎮州大將王德明殺其帥王熔，自稱留後，遣使來求援。
units.en: That month Wang Deming of Zhenzhou murdered Wang Rong, declared himself acting commissioner, and asked for help.
units.literal: That month, Zhenzhou great general Wang Deming killed his commander Wang Rong, styled himself retention commissioner, and sent envoys to seek aid.

units.zh: 宰臣敬翔請許之，租庸使趙岩等以為不可，乃止。
units.en: Jing Xiang favored acceptance; Zhao Yan and others refused, and the court declined.
units.literal: Chief minister Jing Xiang asked to grant it; Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan and others held it impossible, and it stopped.

units.zh: 二月乙巳，王晏球奏，此月三日收復定州，獲王都首級，生擒契丹托諾等二千餘人。
units.en: On yisi in the second month Wang Yanqiu reported recovering Ding on the third, taking Wang Du's head and capturing over two thousand Khitan including Tuonuo alive.
units.literal: Second month, yisi: Wang Yanqiu memorialized that on the third of this month Ding prefecture had been recovered, Wang Du's head was taken, and more than two thousand Khitan including Tuonuo were captured alive.

units.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：尚書兵部宣露布於樓前，宣訖，尚書刑部侍郎張文寶奏曰：「逆賊王都首級請付所司。」
units.en: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says War at the Secretariat proclaimed the bulletin at the tower; when it ended Zhang Wenbao of Punishments asked that Wang Du's head be given to the proper office."
units.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》: The Ministry of War of the Secretariat proclaimed the victory bulletin before the tower; when the proclamation ended, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Zhang Wenbao memorialized: "The rebel Wang Du's head is requested to be delivered to the relevant office."

units.zh: 辛酉，帝御咸安樓受定州俘馘，百官就列，宣露布於樓前，禮畢，以王都首級獻於太社。
units.en: On xinyou Mingzong at the Xian'an Tower received Ding captives, proclaimed the victory bulletin, and offered Wang Du's head at the Grand Shrine.
units.literal: On xinyou, the Emperor took the Xian'an Tower to receive Ding captives and heads; the hundred officials took their places; the victory bulletin was proclaimed before the tower; when the rite was finished, Wang Du's head was offered at the Grand Shrine of State.

units.zh: 王都男四人、弟一人，禿餒父子二人，並磔於市。
units.en: Wang Du's four sons and brother and the Tu Nei father and son were dismembered in the market.
units.literal: Wang Du's four sons, one younger brother, and the father-and-son pair Tu Nei were all dismembered in the market.

units.zh: 大理卿蕭希甫受之以出，獻於郊社，其王都男並蕃將等磔於開封橋。）〉
units.en: Judicial review director Xiao Xifu took it out and offered it at the suburban altars; Wang Du's sons and Tangut generals were dismembered at Kaifeng Bridge.)〉
units.literal: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xiao Xifu received it and went out, offered it at the suburban altars, and Wang Du's sons and the Tangut generals were dismembered at Kaifeng Bridge.)〉

units.zh: 丙申，詔鄴都、幽、鎮、滄、邢、易、定等州管內百姓，除正稅外，放免諸色差配，以討王都之役，有挽運之勞也。
units.en: On bingshen Mingzong remitted extra levies in Yedu, You, Zhen, Cang, Xing, Yi, and Ding beyond regular tax after the Wang Du campaign's transport burden.
units.literal: On bingshen, an edict for the commoners within the circuits of Yedu, You, Zhen, Cang, Xing, Yi, and Ding, besides regular tax, remitted every sort of differential levy, because of the labor of hauling in the campaign against Wang Du.

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·李穀傳》：少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。
units.en: (Biography of Li Gu in the History of Song: when the Young Emperor was driven north in disgrace, former ministers dared not greet him; Gu alone bowed to him on the road, and ruler and subject wept together.
units.literal: (Biography of Li Gu in the History of Song: when the Young Emperor suffered dust on the road north, old ministers dared not wait upon and attend him; Gu alone bowed and welcomed him on the road; ruler and subject faced each other and wept.

units.zh: 〈（《宣政雜錄》：徽宗北狩，經薊縣梁魚務，有還鄉橋，石少帝所命名也，里人至今呼之。）〉
units.en: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng's Reign: when Huizong was taken north he passed Liangyu post in Jixian, where a Returning Home Bridge named by the Shi Young Emperor is still known by that name.)〉
units.literal: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng's Reign: when Huizong went north on the hunt, passing Liangyu post in Jixian, there was a Returning Home Bridge, named by the Young Emperor of Shi; villagers to this day call it so.)〉

units.zh: 記少帝初遷於黃龍府，後居於建州，凡十八年而卒。
units.en: It records that the Young Emperor was first sent to Huanglong, later lived at Jianzhou, and died after eighteen years.
units.literal: It records that the Young Emperor was first moved to Huanglong prefecture, later dwelt at Jianzhou, and after eighteen years in all died.

units.zh: 史臣曰：少帝以中人之才，嗣將墜之業，屬上天不祐，仍歲大饑，尚或絕強敵之歡盟，鄙輔臣之謀略。
units.en: The historian writes: the Young Emperor, a man of middling ability, inherited a dynasty in collapse. Heaven withheld its favor and famine stalked the land year after year; yet he still broke the alliance with a powerful enemy and scorned his ministers' counsel.
units.literal: The historiographer says: the Young Emperor with mediocre talent succeeded a falling enterprise; Heaven did not aid him, famine continued year after year; he still might sever friendly alliance with a strong foe and despise his assisting ministers' stratagems.

units.zh: 《五代史補》：少主之嗣位也，契丹以不俟命而擅立；
units.en: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: when the Young Lord took the throne, the Khitans enthroned him without their leave;
units.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: when the Young Lord succeeded the throne, the Khitans installed him without awaiting command;

units.zh: 而少主方在後苑調鷹，至暮竟不召。
units.en: But the Young Lord was in the rear park training hawks and never summoned him, even by evening.
units.literal: But the Young Lord was just in the rear park training hawks; until evening he was not summoned at all.

units.zh: 未幾，杜重威之徒降於契丹，少主遂北遷。）〉
units.en: Soon Chongwei and his men surrendered to the Khitans, and the Young Lord was driven north.)〉
units.literal: Before long Du Chongwei's party surrendered to the Khitans, and the Young Lord then moved north.)〉

units.zh: 質，石晉末在翰林，為出帝草降表，知其事為詳。
units.en: Zhi served in the Hanlin at the end of Later Jin and drafted the Outgoing Emperor's surrender memorial, so he knew these events in detail.
units.literal: Zhi, at the end of Later Jin was in the Hanlin Academy and drafted the surrender memorial for the Outgoing Emperor; he knew the matter in detail.

units.zh: 〈（《遼史》云：以張彥澤擅徙重貴開封，殺桑維翰，縱兵大掠，不道，斬於市。）〉
units.en: (The History of Liao says Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market for moving Chonggui to Kaifeng on his own authority, killing Sang Weihan, and letting his troops loot the city.)〉
units.literal: (The History of Liao says: because Zhang Yanzhe on his own moved Chonggui to Kaifeng, killed Sang Weihan, and let his troops plunder greatly—unprincipled conduct—he was beheaded in the market.)〉

units.zh: 戊申，日南至，禦崇元殿受朝賀。
units.en: On wushen, the winter solstice, the emperor received New Year court congratulations at the Chongyuan Hall.
units.literal: On wushen, winter solstice, the Emperor took the Chongyuan Hall to receive court congratulations.

units.zh: 前曹州節度使石赟死，帝之堂叔也。
units.en: Former military governor of Caozhou Shi Yun died; he was the emperor's paternal uncle.
units.literal: Former military governor of Caozhou Shi Yun died; he was the Emperor's paternal uncle.

units.zh: 時自中渡寨隔絕之後，帝與大臣端坐憂危，國之衛兵，悉在北面，計無所出。
units.en: Since the Zhongdu camp had been cut off the emperor and his ministers sat helpless in dread; the imperial guards were all in the north and no plan availed.
units.literal: At that time, from after the Zhongdu camp was cut off, the Emperor and the great ministers sat upright in worry and peril; the state's guard troops were all in the north; no plan could be found.

units.zh: 宮中相次火起，帝自攜劍驅擁后妃已下十數人，將同赴火，為親校薛超所持。
units.en: Fires broke out across the palace; the emperor drew his sword and drove the empress, consorts, and a dozen attendants toward the flames to die with them, but his personal guard Xue Chao seized him.
units.literal: Fires broke out one after another in the palace; the Emperor himself took a sword and drove the empress, consorts, and more than ten others below them, intending to enter the fire together; he was seized by his personal officer Xue Chao.

units.zh: 俄自寬仁門遞入契丹主與皇太后書，帝乃止，旋令撲滅煙火。
units.en: Soon a letter from the Khitan lord and the empress dowager was brought in at Kuanren Gate; the emperor desisted and ordered the fires put out.
units.literal: Shortly a letter from the Khitan lord and the Empress Dowager was delivered in at Kuanren Gate; the Emperor then stopped, and immediately ordered the smoke and fire extinguished.

units.zh: 癸酉，帝奉表於戎主曰：
units.en: On guiyou the emperor submitted a memorial to the Khitan lord, saying:
units.literal: On guiyou the Emperor submitted a memorial to the barbarian lord, saying:

units.zh: 甲戌，張彥澤遷帝與太后及諸宮屬於開封府，遣控鶴指揮使李榮將兵監守。
units.en: On jiaxu Zhang Yanzhe moved the emperor, empress dowager, and palace household to the Kaifeng prefectural offices and set Li Rong, commander of the Crane-Control Guard, to watch them with troops.
units.literal: On jiaxu Zhang Yanzhe moved the Emperor, Empress Dowager, and all palace personnel to the Kaifeng prefecture office; he sent Li Rong, commander of the Crane-Control army, to lead troops and guard them.

units.zh: 帝以契丹主將至，欲與太后出迎，彥澤先表之，稟契丹主之旨報云：「比欲許爾朝覲上國，臣僚奏言，豈有兩個天子道路相見！
units.en: When the Khitan lord was expected the emperor wished to go out with the empress dowager to welcome him; Yanzhe reported the Khitan reply: "We meant to let you come to court in the superior state, but your ministers said, How can two Sons of Heaven meet on the road!
units.literal: The Emperor, because the Khitan lord was about to arrive, wished to go out with the Empress Dowager to welcome him; Yanzhe first memorialized, reporting the Khitan lord's order: "We lately wished to permit you to pay court in the superior state; your ministers memorialized, saying, How can two Sons of Heaven meet on the road!

units.zh: 己卯，皇子延煦、延寶自帳中回，得敵詔慰撫，帝表謝之。
units.en: On jimao Princes Yanxu and Yanbao returned from the Khitan camp with a comforting edict, and the emperor sent a memorial of thanks.
units.literal: On jimao the princes Yanxu and Yanbao returned from the enemy camp, received the enemy edict of consolation, and the Emperor submitted a memorial of thanks.

units.zh: 帝進狀曰：「頃以偽主王從珂於洛京大內自焚之後，其真傳國寶不知所在，必是當時焚之。
units.en: The emperor replied: "After the usurper Wang Congke burned himself in the Luoyang palace the true imperial seal was lost and must have perished in that fire.
units.literal: The Emperor submitted a statement: "Lately, after the false ruler Wang Congke burned himself in the great inner palace at Luoyang, the true transmitted state treasure's whereabouts were unknown; it must have been burned at that time.

units.zh: 時移內庫至府，帝使人取帛數段，主者不與，謂使者曰：「此非我所有也。」
units.en: When the inner treasury was moved to the prefectural offices the emperor sent for several bolts of silk; the keeper refused, telling the envoy, "These are no longer mine."
units.literal: At that time the inner treasury was moved to the prefecture office; the Emperor sent men to take several bolts of silk; the custodian would not give them, telling the envoy: "These are not mine to own."

units.zh: 又使人詣李崧求酒，崧曰：「臣有酒非敢愛惜，慮陛下杯酌之後憂躁，所作別有不測之事，臣以此不敢奉進。」
units.en: He also sent to Li Song for wine; Song said, "I have wine and would not begrudge it, but I fear that after you drink in grief you might do something desperate; for that I dare not send it."
units.literal: He also sent men to Li Song to request wine; Song said: "Your subject has wine and would not dare be stingy, but fears that after Your Majesty drinks a cup in worry and agitation you might do something else unforeseen; for this your subject dares not present it."

units.zh: 百官列班，遙辭帝於寺，詣北郊以迎契丹主。
units.en: The officials formed ranks, bade the emperor farewell at the temple from afar, and went to the northern suburb to welcome the Khitan lord.
units.literal: The hundred officials formed ranks, took leave of the Emperor at the temple from afar, and went to the northern suburb to welcome the Khitan lord.

units.zh: 帝舉族出封丘門，肩轝至野，契丹主不與之見，遣泊封禪寺。
units.en: The emperor and his clan went out Fengqiu Gate in litters to the open field; the Khitan lord refused to see them and had them lodged at Fengchan Temple.
units.literal: The Emperor and his whole clan went out Fengqiu Gate, were carried on litters to the open field; the Khitan lord would not meet them and sent them to moor at Fengchan Temple.

units.zh: 辛卯，契丹制，降帝為光祿大夫、檢校太尉，封負義侯，黃龍府安置。
units.en: On xinmao the Khitans demoted the emperor to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Acting Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Bears Guilt, and sent him to Huanglong prefecture.
units.literal: On xinmao by Khitan decree the demoted Emperor was made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Acting Grand Marshal, enfeoffed as Marquis Who Bears Guilt, and settled at Huanglong prefecture.

units.zh: 癸巳，遷帝於封禪寺，遣蕃大將崔廷勛將兵守之。
units.en: On guisi the emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple under guard of the Khitan general Cui Tingxun and his troops.
units.literal: On guisi the Emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple; the barbarian great general Cui Tingxun was sent with troops to guard him.

units.zh: 癸卯，帝與皇太后李氏、皇太妃安氏、皇后馮氏、皇弟重睿、皇子延煦延寶俱北行，以宮嬪五十人、內官三十人、東西班五十人、醫官一人、控鶴官四人、禦廚七人、茶酒三人、儀鸞司三人、軍健二十人從行。
units.en: On guimao the emperor went north with Empress Dowager Li, Grand Imperial Consort An, Empress Feng, his brother Chongrui, and Princes Yanxu and Yanbao, attended by fifty palace women, thirty eunuchs, fifty court attendants, a physician, four Crane-Control officers, seven imperial cooks, three tea and wine servants, three from the Ceremonial Parasol bureau, and twenty guards.
units.literal: On guimao the Emperor with Empress Dowager Lady Li, Grand Imperial Consort Lady An, Empress Lady Feng, younger brother Chongrui, and princes Yanxu and Yanbao all went north together, with fifty palace women, thirty inner eunuchs, fifty eastern and western shift attendants, one medical officer, four Crane-Control officers, seven imperial kitchen staff, three tea and wine servants, three Ceremonial Parasol bureau staff, and twenty military guards accompanying.

units.zh: 宰臣趙瑩、樞密使馮玉、侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜隨帝入蕃，契丹主遣三百騎援送而去。
units.en: Grand Counsellor Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard cavalry, accompanied the emperor into Khitan territory while the Khitan lord sent three hundred horsemen as escort.
units.literal: Grand Counsellor Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and Li Yantao, commander of the Imperial Guard horse army, followed the Emperor into the barbarians; the Khitan lord sent three hundred cavalry to escort and send them off.

units.zh: 嘗一日，帝與太后不能得食，乃殺畜而啖之。
units.en: One day the emperor and empress dowager could get no food and killed livestock to eat.
units.literal: Once on a day the Emperor and Empress Dowager could not obtain food; they then killed livestock and ate it.

units.zh: 帝過中渡橋，閱前杜威營寨之跡，慨然憤嘆，謂左右曰：「我家何負，為此賊所破，天乎！
units.en: Crossing Zhongdu Bridge the emperor looked over Du Wei's old camp, sighed in rage, and said to his attendants, "What had my house done to be ruined by this traitor—O Heaven!
units.literal: The Emperor passed Zhongdu Bridge, reviewed the traces of Du Wei's former camp, sighed in indignant lament, and told those beside him: "What fault has my house, that this bandit broke us—Heaven!

units.zh: 至幽州，傾城士庶迎看於路，見帝慘沮，無不嗟嘆。
units.en: At Youzhou the whole city turned out along the road; seeing the emperor's misery, everyone sighed.
units.literal: Reaching Youzhou, the whole city's gentry and commoners came out on the road to look; seeing the Emperor's wretched dejection, none failed to sigh in lament.

units.zh: 駐留旬餘，州將承契丹命，犒帝於府署，趙延壽母以食饌來獻。
units.en: After more than ten days' halt the prefect, on Khitan orders, entertained the emperor at the prefectural offices, and Zhao Yanshou's mother brought food.
units.literal: They halted more than ten days; the prefectural commander, on Khitan orders, entertained the Emperor at the prefecture office; Zhao Yanshou's mother came to present food.

units.zh: 又行七八日至錦州，契丹迫帝與妃後往拜安巴堅遺像，帝不勝屈辱，泣曰：「薛超誤我，不令我死，以至今日也。」
units.en: Seven or eight days later at Jinzhou the Khitans forced the emperor and his consorts to bow before Ambaqan's portrait; overcome with shame he wept, "Xue Chao was wrong to keep me from death and bring me to this day."
units.literal: After another seven or eight days they reached Jinzhou; the Khitans forced the Emperor and consorts to go pay respects to Ambaqan's portrait; the Emperor could not bear the humiliation and wept: "Xue Chao wronged me, not letting me die, until today."

units.zh: 行至遼陽，皇后馮氏以帝陷蕃，過受艱苦，令內官潛求毒藥，將自飲之，並以進帝，不果而止。
units.en: At Liaoyang Empress Feng, seeing how the emperor suffered in captivity, secretly asked eunuchs for poison to take herself and offer him; the attempt failed and she desisted.
units.literal: Reaching Liaoyang, Empress Lady Feng, because the Emperor had fallen among the barbarians and suffered excessive hardship, had inner eunuchs secretly seek poison, intending to drink it herself and also present it to the Emperor; it did not succeed and she stopped.

units.zh: 又行二百里，會國母為永康王所執，永康王請帝卻往遼陽城駐泊，帝遣使奉表於永康，且賀克捷，自是帝一行稍得供給。
units.en: Two hundred li farther on the Khitan empress dowager was seized by the Prince of Yongkang, who asked the emperor to return to Liaoyang; the emperor sent a memorial congratulating his victory, and thereafter the party received some supplies.
units.literal: After another two hundred li it happened that the empress dowager was seized by the Prince of Yongkang; the Prince of Yongkang asked the Emperor to turn back and moor at Liaoyang city; the Emperor sent envoys submitting a memorial to Yongkang and also congratulating him on victory; from this the Emperor's party slightly obtained supplies.

units.zh: 漢乾祐元年四月，永康王至遼陽，帝與太后並詣帳中，帝御白衣紗帽，永康止之，以常服謁見。
units.en: In the fourth month of Qianyou 1 of Han the Prince of Yongkang reached Liaoyang; the emperor and empress dowager went together to his tent; the emperor came in white robes and a gauze cap, but Yongkang stopped him and received him in ordinary dress.
units.literal: In the fourth month of Han Qianyou 1, the Prince of Yongkang reached Liaoyang; the Emperor and Empress Dowager together went to his tent; the Emperor wore white robes and a gauze cap, but Yongkang stopped him and received him in ordinary dress.

units.zh: 帝伏地雨泣，自陳過咎，永康使左右扶帝上殿，慰勞久之，因命設樂行酒，從容而罷。
units.en: The emperor prostrated himself weeping and confessed his faults; Yongkang had attendants help him into the hall, consoled him at length, ordered music and wine, and dismissed him at ease.
units.literal: The Emperor prostrated himself weeping, confessing his faults; Yongkang had attendants help the Emperor up to the hall, consoled him at length, then ordered music and wine, and dismissed him at ease.

units.zh: 永康帳下從官及教坊內人望見故主，不勝悲咽，內人皆以衣帛藥餌獻遺於帝。
units.en: Yongkang's attendants and palace women of the music bureau saw their former lord and wept; the inner women all presented robes, silks, and medicines to the emperor.
units.literal: Yongkang's attendants and inner women of the music bureau saw their former lord and could not overcome their grief; the inner women all presented robes, silks, and medicines to the Emperor.

units.zh: 有禪奴舍利者，即永康之妻兄也，知帝有小公主在室，詣帝求之，帝辭以年幼不可。
units.en: One Channu Sheli, Yongkang's wife's elder brother, learning the emperor had a young princess at home asked for her; the emperor refused on grounds of her youth.
units.literal: There was one Channu Sheli, Yongkang's wife's elder brother, who knowing the Emperor had a young princess at home came to request her; the Emperor declined on grounds of her youth.

units.zh: 又有東西班數輩善於歌唱，禪奴又請之，帝乃與之。
units.en: Several eastern and western shift attendants skilled at singing were also requested by Channu, and the emperor gave them up.
units.literal: There were also several from the eastern and western shifts skilled at singing whom Channu again requested, and the Emperor gave them up.

units.zh: 後數日，永康王馳取帝幼女而去，以賜綽諾錫裏。
units.en: Several days later the Prince of Yongkang rode off with the emperor's young daughter and gave her to Chuonuo Xili.
units.literal: Several days later the Prince of Yongkang rode off with the Emperor's young daughter and gave her to Chuonuo Xili.

units.zh: 漢乾祐二年二月，帝自遼陽城發赴建州。
units.en: In the second month of Qianyou 2 of Han the emperor left Liaoyang for Jianzhou.
units.literal: In the second month of Han Qianyou 2 the Emperor set out from Liaoyang city for Jianzhou.

units.zh: 帝自遼陽行十數日，過儀州、灞州，遂至建州。
units.en: From Liaoyang the emperor traveled more than ten days through Yizhou and Bazhou to Jianzhou.
units.literal: The Emperor from Liaoyang traveled more than ten days, passed Yizhou and Bazhou, and then reached Jianzhou.

units.zh: 節度使趙延暉盡禮奉迎，館帝於衙署中。
units.en: Military governor Zhao Yanhui received him with full ceremony and lodged the emperor in the prefectural offices.
units.literal: Military governor Zhao Yanhui welcomed him with full ritual courtesy and lodged the Emperor in the prefectural offices.

units.zh: 帝乃令一行人員於寨地內築室分耕，給食於帝。
units.en: The emperor had his party build houses on the land, divide fields for farming, and supply his food.
units.literal: The Emperor then ordered the party within the settlement land to build houses, divide fields, and cultivate, providing food for the Emperor.

units.zh: 是歲，述律王子遣契丹數騎詣帝，取內人趙氏、聶氏疾馳而去。
units.en: That year the prince of Shulü sent Khitan horsemen who seized the palace women Lady Zhao and Lady Nie and rode off with them.
units.literal: That year the prince of Shulü sent several Khitan horsemen to the Emperor, took the inner women Lady Zhao and Lady Nie, and galloped away swiftly.

units.zh: 趙、聶者，帝之寵姬也，及其被奪，不勝悲憤。
units.en: Zhao and Nie were his favorite concubines; when they were taken he was overcome with grief and anger.
units.literal: Zhao and Nie were the Emperor's favored concubines; when they were seized he could not overcome grief and rage.

units.zh: 周顯德初，有漢人自塞北而至者，言帝與後及諸子俱無恙，猶在建州，其隨從職官役使人輩，自蕃中亡歸，物故者大半矣。
units.en: Early in Xiande of Zhou, Han travelers from the northern frontier reported that the emperor, empress, and sons were still alive at Jianzhou; of the officials and servants who escaped from captivity, more than half had perished.
units.literal: At the start of Zhou Xiande, Han people came from north of the passes saying the Emperor, empress, and all sons were unharmed and still at Jianzhou; of the accompanying officials, clerks, and servants who fled back from among the barbarians, more than half had died.

units.zh: 自古亡國之醜者，無如帝之甚也。
units.en: Of all the disgraces of fallen rulers since antiquity, none surpass his.
units.literal: Among disgraces of perished states since antiquity, none match this Emperor's extremity.

units.zh: 明年正月朔，契丹主次東京城北。
units.en: On New Year's Day of the following year the Khitan lord encamped north of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: On the new moon of the first month of the following year the Khitan lord halted north of the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 案：契丹丙午歲入汴，順數至甲子歲為十八年，實太祖乾德二年也。
units.en: Note: the Khitans entered Bian in the bingwu year; counting forward to jiazi gives eighteen years—the year Qiande 2 of Taizu.
units.literal: Note: in the Khitan year bingwu they entered Bian; counting forward to the year jiazi makes eighteen years—actually Taizu's Qiande 2.

units.zh: 癸酉，冊吳國夫人馮氏為皇后。
units.en: On guiyou Lady Feng of Wu was invested as empress.
units.literal: On guiyou Lady Feng of Wu state was invested as empress.

units.zh: 臣與太后並妻馮氏及舉家戚屬，見於郊野面縛俟罪次。
units.en: The empress dowager, my wife Lady Feng, our kin, and I wait bound in the suburbs to receive judgment.
units.literal: Your subject with the Empress Dowager, wife Lady Feng, and all household kin are now in the suburbs, faces bound, awaiting judgment.

units.zh: 旋屬天降鞠兇，先君即世，臣遵承遺旨，纘紹前基。
units.en: Soon Heaven sent cruel misfortune and my father died; I followed his last charge and continued his foundation.
units.literal: Soon it fell to Heaven sending harsh misfortune; the former lord departed the world; your subject followed the testamentary charge and continued the former foundation.

units.zh: 孫臣某言：今月十七日寅時，相州節度使張彥澤、都監傅住兒部領大軍入京，賫到翁皇帝賜太后書示，於滹沱河降下杜重威一行馬步兵士，見領蕃漢步騎來幸汴州者。
units.en: Your grandson-subject reports: at the yin hour on the seventeenth Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Xiangzhou, and chief inspector Fu Zhu'er entered the capital with a great army, bringing the letter the Imperial Father sent the empress dowager; Du Chongwei's horse and foot had surrendered at the Hutuo, and Khitan and Han forces were now marching on Bianzhou.
units.literal: Your grandson-subject speaks: on the seventeenth of this month at the yin hour, Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Xiangzhou, and the chief inspector Fu Zhu'er led a great army into the capital, bearing and displaying the letter the Imperial Father granted the Empress Dowager; at the Hutuo Du Chongwei's party of horse and foot soldiers had surrendered; they are now leading Khitan and Han foot and horse coming to favor Bianzhou.

units.zh: 往者，唐運告終，中原失馭，數窮否極，天缺地傾。
units.en: Formerly Tang's mandate had ended, the Central Plains had lost their helm, fate had reached its nadir, and heaven and earth seemed to collapse.
units.literal: Formerly Tang's mandate ended, the Central Plains lost control, numbers exhausted and obstruction extreme, heaven gapped and earth tilted.

units.zh: 先人有田一成，有眾一旅，兵連禍結，力屈勢孤。
units.en: My forebear held but a patch of land and a single brigade; war piled on disaster until his strength failed and he stood alone.
units.literal: Our forebear had fields one patch, followers one brigade; arms linked with calamity knotted; strength bent, position solitary.

units.zh: 翁皇帝救患摧鋒，興利除害，躬擐甲胄，深入寇場。
units.en: The Imperial Father relieved our distress, broke the enemy spear line, brought benefit and removed harm, donned armor himself, and plunged deep into the enemy country.
units.literal: The Imperial Father rescued distress and crushed spearpoints, raised benefit and removed harm, personally donned armor, and went deep into the bandit field.

units.zh: 犯露蒙霜，度雁門之險；
units.en: Braving dew and frost he crossed the peril of Yanmen Pass;
units.literal: Braving dew and shrouded in frost, he crossed the peril of Yanmen;

units.zh: 馳風掣電，行中冀之誅。
units.en: riding like wind and lightning he carried out judgment in central Ji.
units.literal: wind-chasing, lightning-snatching, he executed punishment in central Ji.

units.zh: 黃鉞一麾，天下大定。
units.en: One wave of the imperial axe and the realm was settled.
units.literal: With one wave of the yellow battle-axe, all under Heaven was greatly settled.

units.zh: 勢淩宇宙，義感神明，功成不居，遂興晉祚，則翁皇帝有大造於石氏也。
units.en: His power spanned the cosmos and his righteousness moved the gods; when his task was done he did not keep the glory but raised the Jin throne—thus the Imperial Father wrought the greatest service for the house of Shi.
units.literal: His power overrode cosmos; his righteousness moved spirits; achievement complete he did not dwell on it; he then raised the Jin mandate—thus the Imperial Father had great creating merit toward the Shi clan.

units.zh: 諒暗之初，荒迷失次，凡有軍國重事，皆委將相大臣。
units.en: In the first days of mourning I was lost and disordered; all grave matters of state I left to my generals and ministers.
units.literal: At the start of deep mourning I was lost and out of order; all weighty affairs of army and state were entrusted to generals and ministers.

units.zh: 至於擅繼宗祧，既非稟命；
units.en: As for seizing the succession without your command,
units.literal: As for usurping succession to the ancestral temple, it was not by received command;

units.zh: 輕發文字，輒敢抗尊。
units.en: they issued documents lightly and dared defy your authority.
units.literal: lightly issuing documents, they dared resist your exalted person.

units.zh: 自啟釁端，果貽赫怒，禍至神惑，運盡天亡。
units.en: They provoked conflict and brought your wrath; disaster came, the spirits were confounded, and our mandate was spent.
units.literal: They themselves opened the provocation; truly they brought your blazing wrath; calamity arrived, spirits were confused, fortune exhausted, Heaven's mandate perished.

units.zh: 十萬師徒，皆望風而束手；
units.en: A hundred thousand soldiers all laid down their arms at the first wind;
units.literal: A hundred thousand troops all looked to the wind and bound their hands;

units.zh: 億兆黎庶，悉延頸以歸心。
units.en: and the people everywhere craned their necks in submission.
units.literal: hundreds of millions of common people all stretched their necks to turn their hearts.

units.zh: 臣負義包羞，貪生忍恥，自貽顛覆，上累祖宗，偷度晨昏，茍存食息。
units.en: I bear shame and disgrace, clinging to life; I brought ruin on myself and burdened my ancestors, stealing through each day merely to breathe.
units.literal: Your subject bears righteousness wrapped in shame, clings to life and endures disgrace, himself brings downfall, above burdens the ancestors, steals through dawn and dusk, barely preserves breath and food.

units.zh: 翁皇帝若惠顧疇昔，稍霽雷霆，未賜靈誅，不絕先祀，則百口荷更生之德，一門銜無報之恩，雖所願焉，非敢望也。
units.en: If the Imperial Father would look kindly on past ties, temper his wrath, spare us execution, and let our ancestral rites continue, a hundred mouths would owe you reborn life and our whole clan a debt we could never repay—this is our hope, though we dare not expect it.
units.literal: If the Imperial Father in kindness looks to former days, slightly clears his thunder, does not grant spirit punishment, does not cut off ancestral sacrifices, then a hundred mouths would bear the virtue of renewed life, one clan would hold gratitude beyond repayment—though this is what we wish, we dare not expect it.

units.zh: 所有國寶一面、金印三面，今遣長子陜府節度使延煦、次子曹州節度使延寶管押進納，並奉表請罪，陳謝以聞。
units.en: I send the state seal and three gold seals under escort of my eldest son Yanxu, military governor of Shan, and my second son Yanbao, military governor of Caozhou, with this memorial begging your pardon.
units.literal: The state treasure one face and gold seals three faces—now your eldest son Yanxu, military governor of Shan prefecture circuit, and second son Yanbao, military governor of Caozhou, are sent to escort and present them, together submitting this memorial begging pardon, declaring apology for your hearing.

units.zh: 又行數十程，渡遼水，至黃龍府，即此所命安置之地也。
units.en: After many more stages they crossed the Liao and reached Huanglong prefecture, the place where he had been ordered to live.
units.literal: After another several tens of stages they crossed the Liao River and reached Huanglong prefecture—this was the place appointed for their settlement.

units.zh: 族行萬里，身老窮荒。
units.en: His clan was driven ten thousand li; he grew old in a barren land.
units.literal: His clan traveled ten thousand li; his person aged in desolate wilds.

units.zh: 奢淫自縱，謂有泰山之安；
units.en: He gave himself to luxury and excess, believing his throne as secure as Mount Tai;
units.literal: Luxurious and licentious, he indulged himself, thinking he had Mount Tai's security;

units.zh: 委托非人，坐受平陽之辱。
units.en: he entrusted power to the wrong men and suffered the disgrace of Pingyang while doing nothing.
units.literal: he entrusted the wrong men and sat receiving the disgrace of Pingyang.

units.zh: 戊寅，契丹阿保機遣使貢良馬。
units.en: On wuyin Abaoji sent fine horses as tribute.
units.literal: On wuyin the Khitan Abaoji sent envoys presenting fine horses.

units.zh: 領生耨里思，大度寡欲，令不嚴而人化，是為肅祖。
units.en: Ling's son Noulisi was broad-minded and sparing in wants; though his rule was mild, the people were naturally swayed—this was Emperor Suzu.
units.literal: Ling begot Noulisi, who was magnanimous and few in desires; his orders were not strict yet the people were transformed—he is known as Emperor Suzu.

units.zh: 肅祖生薩剌德，嘗與黃室韋挑戰，矢貫數劄，是為懿祖。
units.en: Suzu had Salade, who once duelled the Yellow Shiwei; arrows ran through stack upon stack of quivers—this was Emperor Yizu.
units.literal: Suzu begot Salade, who once fought the Yellow Shiwei in battle; arrows pierced through several quivers—he is known as Emperor Yizu.

units.zh: 夏五月丙寅，吳越王復遣滕彥休貢犀角、珊瑚，授官以遣。
units.en: In the fifth month of summer, on bingyin day, the King of Wuyue again dispatched Teng Yanxiu with rhinoceros horn and coral as tribute; he was granted an office and sent home.
units.literal: In the fifth month of summer, on bingyin day, the King of Wuyue again sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute of rhinoceros horn and coral; offices were conferred on him and he was sent away.

units.zh: 時鎮州王熔、定州王處直叛，結連晉人，故遣將討之。
units.en: Wang Rong of Zhenzhou and Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou had rebelled and joined the Jin, so troops were sent against them.
units.literal: At the time Zhenzhou’s Wang Rong and Dingzhou’s Wang Chuzhi had rebelled and allied with the Jin, so generals were sent to attack them.

units.zh: 矧又王熔、處直未曾削爵除名，若翻然改圖，不遠而復，必仍舊貫，當保前功。
units.en: Wang Rong and Chuzhi have not been stripped of rank; if they turn back soon, they keep their posts and their past merit.
units.literal: Moreover Wang Rong and Chuzhi have not yet been stripped of rank and name—if they turn back and return not far off, they shall keep their old posts and preserve their former merit.

units.zh: <九>以后弟阿骨只為統軍，實魯為先鋒，東出關略燕、趙，不遇敵而還。
units.en: <9> The empress's younger brother Aguzhi was made commander-in-chief with Shilu as vanguard; marching east out of the pass he raided Yan and Zhao, met no enemy, and returned.
units.literal: <9> The Empress's younger brother Aguzhi was made commander-in-chief and Shilu vanguard; marching east out of the pass he raided Yan and Zhao, met no enemy, and returned.

units.zh: 癸亥，城皇都，以禮部尚書康默記充版築使。
